prompt: An eight-year-old reads familiar stories from context, but after sustained instruction still cannot decode unfamiliar words and avoids reading aloud. A teacher says normal-looking MRI rules out a reading disorder, so the family should just wait. How should we respond?

criteria.boundary: Rejects normal MRI as sufficient to exclude a reading disorder; distinguishes context guessing from decoding.
criteria.action: Recommends timely qualified educational/clinical reading assessment and targeted support, without diagnosing the child or waiting for proof of a lesion.

note: New scenario after original mirrors final case missed actionable qualified-assessment criterion; original case retained as a failed probe, not rerun as an untouched holdout.
